1.1: The burden that Habakkuk the prophet has seen:
1.2: Till when, O Jehovah, have I cried, And You do not hear? I cry to You--`Violence,' and You do not save.
1.3: Why do You show me iniquity, And perversity do cause to behold? And spoiling and violence are before me, And there is strife, and contention does lift itself up,
1.4: Therefore does law cease, And judgment does not go forth for ever, For the wicked is compassing the righteous, Therefore wrong judgment goes forth.
1.5: Look you on nations, and behold and marvel greatly. For a work He is working in your days, You do not believe though it is declared.
1.6: For, indeed, I am raising up the Chaldeans, The bitter and hasty nation, That is going to the broad places of earth, To occupy tabernacles not its own.
1.7: Terrible and fearful it is, From itself its judgment and its excellency go forth.
1.8: Swifter than leopards have been its horses, And sharper than evening wolves, And increased have its horsemen, Even its horsemen from afar come in, They fly as an eagle, hasting to consume.
1.9: Wholly for violence it does come in, Their faces swallowing up the east wind, And it does gather as the sand a captivity.
1.10: And at kings it does scoff, And princes are a laughter to it, At every fenced place it does laugh, And it heaps up dust, and captures it.
1.11: Then passed on has the spirit, Yes, he does transgress, And does ascribe this his power to his god.
1.12: Are not You of old, O Jehovah, my God, my Holy One? We do not die, O Jehovah, For judgment You have appointed it, And, O Rock, for reproof You have founded it.
1.13: Purer of eyes than to behold evil, To look on perverseness You are not able, Why do You behold the treacherous? You keep silent when the wicked Does swallow the more righteous than he,
1.14: And You make man as fishes of the sea, As a creeping thing--none ruling over him.
1.15: Each of them with a hook he has brought up, He does catch it in his net, and gathers it in his drag, Therefore he does joy and rejoice.
1.16: Therefore he does sacrifice to his net, And does make perfume to his drag, For by them is his portion fertile, and his food fat.
1.17: Does he therefore empty his net, And continually to slay nations spare not?

2.1: On my charge I stand, and I station myself on a bulwark, and I watch to see what He does speak against me, and what I do reply to my reproof.
2.2: And Jehovah answers me and says: `Write a vision, and explain on the tables, That he may run who is reading it.
2.3: For yet the vision is for a season, And it breathes for the end, and does not lie, If it tarry, wait for it, For surely it comes, it is not late.
2.4: Indeed, a presumptuous one! Not upright is his soul within him, And the righteous by his stedfastness lives.
2.5: And also, because the wine is treacherous, A man is haughty, and remains not at home, Who has enlarged as sheol his soul, And is as death that is not satisfied, And does gather to itself all the nations, And does assemble to itself all the peoples,
2.6: Do not these--all of them--against him a simile taken up, And a moral of acute sayings for him, And say, Woe to him who is multiplying what is not his? Till when also is he multiplying to himself heavy pledges?
2.7: Do not your usurers instantly rise up, And those shaking you awake up, And you have been for a spoil to them?
2.8: Because you have spoiled many nations, Spoil you do all the remnant of the peoples, Because of man's blood, and of violence to the land, To the city, and to all dwelling in it.
2.9: Woe to him who is gaining evil gain for his house, To set on high his nest, To be delivered from the hand of evil,
2.10: You have counselled a shameful thing to your house, To cut off many peoples, and sinful is your soul.
2.11: For a stone from the wall does cry out, And a holdfast from the wood answers it.
2.12: Woe to him who is building a city by blood, And establishing a city by iniquity.
2.13: Indeed, is it not from Jehovah of Hosts And peoples are fatigued for fire, And nations for vanity are weary?
2.14: For full is the earth of the knowledge of the honour of Jehovah, As waters cover the bottom of a sea.
2.15: Woe to him who is giving drink to his neighbour, Pouring out your bottle, and also making drunk, In order to look on their nakedness.
2.16: You have been filled--shame without honour, Drink you also, and be uncircumcised, Turn round to you does the cup of the right hand of Jehovah, And shameful spewing is on your honour.
2.17: For violence to Lebanon does cover you, And spoil of beasts does affright them, Because of man's blood, and of violence to the land, To the city, and to all dwelling in it.
2.18: What profit has a graven image given That its former has graven it? A molten image and teacher of falsehood, That trusted has the former on his own formation--to make dumb idols?
2.19: Woe to him who is saying to wood, `Awake,' `Stir up,' to a dumb stone, It a teacher! indeed, it is overlaid--gold and silver, And there is no spirit in its midst.
2.20: And Jehovah is in His holy temple, Be silent before Him, all the earth!

3.1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet concerning erring ones:
3.2: O Jehovah, I heard your report, I have been afraid, O Jehovah, Your work! in midst of years revive it, In the midst of years You make known In anger You do remember mercy.
3.3: God from Teman does come, The Holy One from mount Paran. Pause! Covered the heavens has His majesty, And His praise has filled the earth.
3.4: And the brightness is as the light, He has rays out of His hand, And there--the hiding of His strength.
3.5: Before Him goes pestilence, And a burning flame goes forth at His feet.
3.6: He has stood, and He measures earth, He has seen, and He shakes off nations, And scatter themselves do mountains of antiquity, Bowed have the hills of old, The ways of old are His.
3.7: Under sorrow I have seen tents of Cushan, Tremble do curtains of the land of Midian.
3.8: Against rivers has Jehovah been wroth? Against rivers is Yours anger? Against the sea is Your wrath? For You do ride on Your horses--Your chariots of salvation?
3.9: Utterly naked You do make Your bow, Sworn are the tribes--saying, `Pause!' With rivers You do cleave the earth.
3.10: Seen you--pained are mountains, An inundation of waters has passed over, Given forth has the deep its voice, High its hands it has lifted up.
3.11: Sun--moon--has stood--a habitation, At the light your arrows go on, At the brightness, the glittering of your spear.
3.12: In indignation You do tread earth, In anger You do thresh nations.
3.13: You have gone forth for the salvation of Your people, For salvation with Your anointed, You have smitten the head of the house of the wicked, Laying bare the foundation to the neck. Pause!
3.14: You have pierced with his staves the head of his leaders, They are tempestuous to scatter me, Their exultation is as to consume the poor in secret.
3.15: You have proceeded through the sea with Your horses--the clay of many waters.
3.16: I have heard, and my belly trembles, At the noise have my lips quivered, Rottenness does come into my bones, And in my place I do tremble, That I rest for a day of distress, At the coming up of the people, he overcomes it.
3.17: Though the fig-tree does not flourish, And there is no produce among vines, Failed has the work of the olive, And fields have not yielded food, Cut off from the fold has been the flock, And there is no herd in the stalls.
3.18: Yet I, in Jehovah I exult, I do joy in the God of my salvation.
3.19: Jehovah the Lord is my strength, And He does make my feet like hinds, And on my high-places causes me to tread. To the overseer with my stringed instruments!
